LESSON: LINEAR INEQUALITIES

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: GRADE
Strand: ALGEBRA
Topic 2.3: Linear Inequalities
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Linear Inequalities, part of ALGEBRA in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven GRADE.

Key inquiry question: How do we use linear inequalities in real life? 2. Why do we use linear inequalities in real life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Linear Inequalities together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: Observing and signing; as the learner participates in the discussion on how to

form the linear inequalities.

● Creativity and imagination: Uses creativity in work context; as the learner draws and represents inequality

statements on a number line.

Values:
● Unity: As the learner cooperates in using inequality cards to complete compound inequality statements.

● Love: As the learner shares inequality cards while completing compound inequality statements.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

● Health Promotion Issues: Drugs and substance abuse; Observing the correct dosage in drugs / limits on drug

consumption.

● Socio-Economic and Environmental Issues: Gender issues; Gender representation for inclusivity.

Link to other learning areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept of inequality to describe acceptable ranges of vital signs or dosage limits for

medications in Integrated Science.

Suggested Learning Resources:
